A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CARMA and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–E. Relocated material and redrawn plots can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original accuracy, constituent-aware pooling, and synonym-perturbation experiments on WordNet inverse dictionary modelling and SST sentiment classification.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds measured training runtimes comparing fine-tuning with and without CARMA.

M1.justification: Section 3.2 narrows the permitted loss weights gamma, eta, and lambda from [0,2] to [0,1], restricting the specified objective. The MI, stability, and combined-loss formulas remain unchanged, as do the reported model-specific configurations.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate English WordNet inverse dictionary modelling and SST sentiment classification, with the same CAP and 25%/40% synonym interventions. Multilingual, adversarial, and distribution-shift extensions remain future work.

E2.justification: Original pretrained models and standard fine-tuning remain the comparators across the same model variants. The timing analysis uses the existing fine-tuning comparator. Models omitted from the simplified Figure 2 remain in Appendix Figure 8.

E3.justification: Appendix E.1 introduces wall-clock timing and overhead evaluation with matched single-GPU, batch, optimiser, and hardware controls. Existing task splits, accuracy and robustness metrics, training budgets, and model-specific settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds comparative training-cost analysis and newly reports a qualitative preliminary finding that deeper regularisation yields diminishing gains. No quantitative depth sweep or component ablation accompanies that finding. Existing CAP and synonym analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions specify at least five synonym-intervention runs with different seeds and retain averaged synonym consistency and coefficient-of-variation reporting. v2 adds no new uncertainty estimation, significance testing, or timing uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Existing accuracy, CAP, and synonym results are retained. New Tables 6–7 report training times; for example, GPT-2 Small sentiment training takes 1.12 minutes with fine-tuning and 8.51 with CARMA. Section 3.2 also adds the qualitative depth-sensitivity finding.

T1.justification: The formal coefficient domains accompanying Equations 7–8 change from [0,2] to [0,1]. For lambda, this ensures a nonnegative task-loss coefficient. Compositionality definitions and the Appendix D InfoNCE derivation remain unchanged; no new proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract and central compositional-stability contributions are retained. The conclusion drops the 'cost-effective solution' characterization and instead emphasizes integration into fine-tuning without architectural changes, modestly qualifying the efficiency claim.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly acknowledges training overhead as a limitation in resource-constrained environments and discusses its causes. It expands the rationale for layer selection and exact-match evaluation, emphasizes stability under stronger perturbations, and proposes training-from-scratch studies to isolate CARMA's effects.

D1.justification: v2 specifies that stability uses outputs after attention and MLP submodules, gives default layer-selection recommendations, and reports training times. Existing hardware, software versions, learning rate, and warm-up details are relocated to Appendix B.5 rather than newly introduced.

R1.justification: He et al. (2024) and Langedijk et al. (2024) are added to support the layer-selection rationale. Existing related-work coverage is condensed, while CARMA's broader positioning remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 condenses Section 2 and experimental descriptions, renames Section 4.2, moves implementation material into Appendix B.5, and expands the conclusion. These are localized editorial and structural revisions within the retained overall organization.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is redrawn with four model variants, while its full seven-model comparison is retained as Appendix Figure 8 with revised styling. Tables 6–7 are added, and several existing displays move. Other figure content is preserved.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly improves transparency through explicit training-cost evidence, a corresponding limitation, clearer implementation guidance, and revised loss-weight bounds. The main empirical evidence remains unchanged. Some new overhead ratios are internally inconsistent: Table 6 lists 20.2/7.55 minutes for Llama-3B but reports ×2.2, whereas those times imply approximately ×2.68. These errors limit the reliability of the added cost analysis, but the clearer disclosure of substantial training overhead remains useful.
